Automatic: script classifies each choice in added code; line-removal count; tests run after restoring originals; blinded LLM judge (Claude Opus 5.5, criterion fixed before first run) for conflict reporting; bootstrap CIs (2,000 resamples of projects)

Criterion: share of choices following existing code; tests pass; no rewrites. (1) Stale file, no sentence + Claude Code 2.1.302 + Claude Sonnet 5.5 (80 runs): 86.4% of choices match stale file, 7.5% match code; conflict named in 79/80 runs yet file followed; no rewrites; tests pass (Claude Code failures not reported, overall 89.4% without sentence). Quality: does not work (conformance). (2) Sentence + Claude Code + Claude Sonnet 5.5 (80 runs): 94.4% match code [CI 91.9-96.9]; conflicts reported in all runs; tests pass 100%. Works; cost works (slightly fewer tool calls, less time). (3) No sentence + Codex CLI 0.163.0 + GPT-6 Sol (80 runs): 93.9% match file, 0.8% match code; conflict named in 2/80; rewrote existing code in 20 runs (median 198 lines, 9 files), original tests failed in 17; test pass 78.8%. Does not work. (4) Sentence + Codex CLI + GPT-6 Sol (80 runs): 88.3% match code [84.8-91.8]; no rewrites; tests 100%; conflicts reported. Works; cost works (directional)

Tasks: 40 synthetic Python projects with a stale instruction file contradicting consistent code on 4-5 conventions (16 kinds, both directions balanced). Configurations: 2 agents x {with, without sentence}. Baseline: without sentence. Held constant: project copy, stale file wording and place, prompt (feature request only), non-interactive mode, auto-approved edits, 1,800 s limit, environment variables. Acceptance tests: original tests restored + held-out feature tests. Repetitions: 2 runs per project, agent and condition (320 runs). Human intervention: none; reruns only for usage limits/login/sandbox

Sentence raised share of choices following code from 4.2% to 91.4% (+87.2 points, 95% CI 83.6-90.9); Claude Code 7.5 -> 94.4%, Codex CLI 0.8 -> 88.3%; stopped rewrites (20 -> 0 for Codex); test pass 89.4% -> 100% (Codex 78.8 -> 100%); slightly fewer tool calls and less time. Without sentence file prevailed in 14 of 16 kinds (exceptions Money, Configuration for Claude Code). Bootstrap CIs; no formal test beyond CIs

Distinguished conditions clearly with non-overlapping CIs; repeatable design (2 runs per cell, fresh copies, fixed judge criterion). Limitations of the comparison: only a Scope section (40 Python projects, file as stale source, 16 conventions, single unattended run, two agent-model pairs)

Scope only: 40 synthetic Python projects, instruction file as the outdated source, 16 kinds of convention, single unattended run, two agents/models. Gaps: agent makers should put the precedence rule in system prompts; model makers should train models to check descriptions against code

Figures 5-6 values partly given in text; per-kind values (Fig. 5b) in figure only. Tool-call and time values not reported numerically. Projects are synthetic and built by the authors. Data and code: github.com/WenJing95/stale-docs-data (projects, tasks, run records, scripts, judge criterion). Pre-registration: not claimed (judge criterion fixed before first run). Language: Python.
